analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a documentation paragraph at lines 1293-1298 describing PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup. That paragraph says the lookup snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between its two bounded generations, so a promotion that rotates the cache cannot turn a later piece in the same lookup into a miss. It also says token arrays share storage during the snapshot, existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. No source code, config, protocol or threat-model files are in the supplied evidence, so no control is added, removed or weakened by anything I could see. Relevant threat context is T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache and TTFT oracle). The documented prompt-piece token cache is scoped per prefix-cache scope (line ~1292, 'Reuse never crosses a cache scope'), and the change preserves that statement. The snapshot-before-promote behavior is a correctness and latency fix. It could slightly change hit/miss timing within a single request, but it adds no cross-scope or cross-tenant exposure, and the same-account timing oracle is already the accepted risk SEC-035. Remaining unverified contract: the real implementation of PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup (snapshot semantics, memory bounds with shared storage, scope keying) is not supplied. A next pass should confirm the code matches the docs: scope isolation is retained, byte bounds are enforced, and snapshot sharing does not alias mutable state across scopes. This is a documentation-only change, so I report no findings.
